import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures in Complexity Theory

This file contains formal statements of some of the main open conjectures
in complexity theory, including

- the P vs NP problem
- the NP vs coNP problem

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P_versus_NP_problem)
- [The Clay Institute](https://www.claymath.org/millennium/p-vs-np/)
-/

namespace ComplexityTheory

/--
**P ≠ NP**:

The conjecture that the complexity classes P and NP are not equal.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 68]
theorem P_ne_NP : P ≠ NP := by sorry

/--
**NP ≠ coNP**:

The conjecture that the complexity classes NP and coNP are not equal.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 68]
theorem NP_ne_coNP : NP ≠ coNP := by sorry

/--
The theorem that the set of complements of languages in P is itself P.

This can be proven by observing that the boolean negation function is computable in polynomial time,
and that compositions of poly-time computable functions are also poly-time computable.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 68]
theorem coP_eq_P :
    { L | Lᶜ ∈ P } = P := by
  sorry

/--
The theorem that P is a subset of NP.

This can be proven by observing that for any language in P,
we can construct a verifier that ignores the witness and simply runs the poly-time decider for the
language.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 68]
theorem P_subset_NP :
    P ⊆ NP := by
  sorry

/--
The theorem that P is a subset of coNP.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 68]
theorem P_subset_coNP :
    P ⊆ coNP := by
  rw [coNP, ← coP_eq_P]
  simp only [Set.ofPred_subset_ofPred]
  intros L hL
  exact P_subset_NP hL

end ComplexityTheory

reformulations.difference: The imported classes use Boolean characteristic functions, self-delimiting binary encodings, and finite multi-stack machines. The NP definition allows witnesses of length at most a polynomial, rather than the exact-length convention in Arora–Barak Definition 2.1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Characteristic functions correspond bijectively to binary languages, and Cook explicitly states independence from the fixed alphabet size when it is at least two. The actual encodings have lengths 3|x| and 6|x|+3|w|+1 and are linearly transcodable with ordinary string encodings. The stack-machine model is polynomially equivalent to ordinary Turing machines: control and program syntax are finite, and even work alphabets without explicit finiteness fields have only finitely many reachable symbols, since push operations have finite state domains. Macro-step counting and cleanup to the required final configuration preserve polynomial time. Exact-length and bounded-length certificates interconvert using self-delimiting padding to 2p(n)+1 bits and, in the reverse direction, an explicit length guard. These choices therefore leave P and NP unchanged. The same analysis applies to NP_ne_coNP.

reformulations.difference: The source describes closure under complementation, while Lean states that the preimage of P under language complementation equals P.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Complementation is involutive. For any class C, closure L ∈ C → Lᶜ ∈ C implies Lᶜ ∈ C ↔ L ∈ C by applying closure twice, and hence {L | Lᶜ ∈ C} = C. Conversely, that equality immediately implies closure. The preimage also equals the image under complementation, matching the docstring's 'set of complements' wording. Both equivalences were proved in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: Stephen Cook, The P Versus NP Problem, especially §1, pp. 5–7, and the machine appendix: https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/pvsnp.pdf

Sanjeev Arora and Boaz Barak, Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach, online draft, Definitions 1.20 and 2.1, Claim 2.3, Theorem 2.6, and §2.6.1: https://theory.cs.princeton.edu/complexity/book.pdf
Local definitions at the reviewed commit: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Computability/Complexity.lean and FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Computability/BitstringEncoding.lean.

review.notes: Checked all five declarations and their supporting definitions. Both separation conjectures remain open in the consulted sources; the three background facts are appropriately tagged textbook. No answer(...) or formal_proof records occur. Successful Lean checks cover Boolean coercions and complements, encoding lengths and smallest inputs, zero witness bounds, and impossibility of a zero-step computation reaching the required halt configuration. Explicit constant-output machines prove that the empty and universal languages belong to P, NP, and coNP without using any admitted problem theorem; their proofs contain no sorryAx.
